description: issue #688 (terminal slice, review round 1): the `ONLY within` half of `spec/interaction-events.md:43-47` as that section read when this fixture was written -- `An implementation that does not declare this profile does not reserve those words except through a vendor extension or an imported alias.` This is the byte-identical source its twin `block-heads-reserved-under-profile` runs under an ACTIVE profile, checked here with Core Language alone: all four names are ordinary, definable procedure names and the program checks CLEAN, with zero diagnostics. The pair is what made the reservation PROFILE-SCOPED rather than global -- either fixture alone is satisfied by an implementation that reserves the four words unconditionally (failing learners on a Core-only program that legitimately defines a procedure called `every`) or by one that never reserves them at all. SCOPE, CORRECTED: maintainer ruling #833 RETRACTED the `only within` half. `spec/grammar.md:408` makes profile words built-in names unconditionally -- what a profile decides is whether a name WORKS, never whether a program may declare it -- and issue #855 aligned `spec/interaction-events.md:43-47` with it, so the sentence quoted above is no longer in the spec. This fixture therefore pins SHIPPED BEHAVIOUR that the spec now contradicts: a conforming 0.4.0 implementation must raise `ol-reserved-word` here. It is kept, red-flagged, so the behaviour is not silently unpinned; issue #841 lands the always-on built-in-names list and flips this fixture's expectation. This is a check-mode fixture: it proves static legality only and does not execute.
